historical_commentary.text: This note explores how 4D v6's new Form Events model handles event inheritance (across forms/objects) and how understanding that model can be used to optimize database performance; the specific V6-era Events architecture described has since been extended with many more event types and refined semantics in later 4D versions, though the general principle of using event-driven logic thoughtfully to avoid unnecessary work remains conceptually relevant today.
related_updates: 4D's Form Events model (introduced in v6, replacing the earlier Phases terminology) has been substantially expanded with additional event types and refined semantics across many subsequent 4D versions
Performance optimization techniques tied to event handling have evolved alongside 4D's broader move toward multi-process, multi-threaded, and ORDA-based architectures
